31. Verify that pagination controls navigate correctly between pages of results.
32. Verify that the "Next" and "Previous" pagination buttons are disabled appropriately on the first and last pages.
33. Verify that sort order toggles between ascending and descending correctly.
34. Verify that sorting persists when navigating away from and back to the list page.
35. Verify that data displayed in list views matches the records stored in the database.
36. Verify that create, read, update, and delete (CRUD) operations work for each major data entity.

44. Verify that uploaded files can be downloaded by authorized users.
45. Verify that uploaded images are displayed correctly in thumbnail views.

48. Verify that form submissions are idempotent where required, preventing duplicate records on double-click or network retry.

59. Verify that the application handles concurrent edits to the same record gracefully.

62. Verify that successful payment transactions update the order status in the database.
63. Verify that failed payment transactions do not create an order record.
64. Verify that partial refunds are processed correctly through the payment gateway.
65. Verify that the application correctly consumes a third-party REST API and handles the documented response format.

## Usability and Accessibility Testing Scenarios

126. Verify that the application is fully navigable using only the keyboard.
127. Verify that a visible focus indicator is present on all interactive elements.

135. Verify that the layout is responsive and adapts to desktop, tablet, and mobile screen sizes.

## Performance Testing Scenarios

151. Verify that the homepage loads within the acceptable performance budget under normal conditions.
152. Verify that the application handles the expected number of concurrent users without degradation.
153. Verify that API response times remain within acceptable limits under peak load.
154. Verify that database queries execute within acceptable time thresholds.

185. Verify that all numeric fields reject non-numeric input.

196. Verify that database migrations run without data loss during upgrades.
197. Verify that rollback procedures restore the previous state if a migration fails.
198. Verify that audit logs record all create, update, and delete operations with timestamps.
199. Verify that audit logs cannot be modified by regular users.
200. Verify that data archiving jobs move old records to cold storage without breaking references.
201. Verify that user preferences persist across sessions and devices when designed to do so.
202. Verify that shopping cart contents persist across sessions for logged-in users.
203. Verify that inventory counts are decremented atomically when orders are placed.
204. Verify that promotional codes can only be used the configured number of times.
205. Verify that subscription renewals are processed on the correct dates.
206. Verify that cancellation of a subscription takes effect at the end of the billing period.
207. Verify that prorated charges are calculated correctly for mid-cycle subscription changes.

## Recovery, Failover, and Edge Cases

208. Verify that the application displays a friendly error page when the database is unreachable.
209. Verify that the application retries transient network failures automatically.
210. Verify that data entered before a network interruption is not lost when connectivity is restored.
211. Verify that the system can be restored from the most recent backup within the recovery time objective.
212. Verify that point-in-time recovery restores the database to the correct state.
213. Verify that the standby database takes over automatically when the primary database fails.
214. Verify that queued jobs are processed once the system recovers from an outage.
215. Verify that scheduled reports are generated even if the server restarts during the scheduled window.
216. Verify that the application handles empty states gracefully, such as an empty inbox or empty dashboard.
217. Verify that the application handles extremely long input strings without truncation or layout breakage.
218. Verify that the application handles special characters and emoji in text inputs.
219. Verify that the application handles copy-paste of formatted text into rich text editors.
220. Verify that the application handles rapid successive clicks on action buttons without duplicate actions.
221. Verify that the application handles browser window resizing without breaking the layout.
222. Verify that the application handles offline mode with appropriate messaging and queued actions.
223. Verify that the application handles clock skew between client and server gracefully.
224. Verify that the application handles very large numbers in numeric fields without overflow.
225. Verify that the application handles null and undefined values gracefully throughout the stack.
226. Verify that the application handles simultaneous updates from multiple users on shared data.
227. Verify that the application handles expired sessions during long form completion.
228. Verify that the application handles browser crashes and restores unsaved work where feasible.
229. Verify that the application handles deep links to content that requires authentication.
230. Verify that the application handles URLs with special characters and query parameters correctly.

This list covers more than 200 scenarios spanning the full quality lifecycle. Each scenario can be expanded into explicit test cases with preconditions, steps, test data, and expected results based on your specific application requirements and acceptance criteria.
